summary: Demo and migration walkthrough focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together APIs to Redwood API, Console walkthrough (routes, model pinning, rollouts), and Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization). Customer concerned about latency, cost, SSO and data residency. Agreed PoC benchmark and security docs share.
topics: Optimize: batching, KV caching, quantization suggestions
transcript: 00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna walk through how to map your current OpenAI/Anthropic/Together usage to Redwood, and demo the console and optimize toolkit. uh priya's gonna run through the technical bits. 00:18 Priya (Redwood SE): cool, thanks jordan. michelle? michael? 00:21 Michael (Customer - CTO): yeah this is michael, sorry audio was a bit delayed. 00:27 Jordan: no worries. quick pre-qual - can you remind us of your current stack? you're on OpenAI for chat, Anthropic for LLM safety checks, and Together for some internal models? 00:38 Laura (Customer): yep we use openai gpt-4o for product summaries, anthropic for safety/rerank, and together for a cheaper embedding pipeline. 00:48 Priya: sounds familiar. first point of parity: api request shapes. openai-style calls map to /v1/generate and /v1/chat on redwood, parameters like temperature, top_p, max_tokens map directly, but note: our top_p defaults and token accounting differ slightly. 01:06 Michael: ok, what about streaming? we rely on streaming in prod. 01:10 Priya: we support streaming. small transcription note: sometimes streaming event names differ - in our SDK it's streamDelta events; you'll see slight naming diffs, but logic is same. 01:20 Samir (Customer): function calling? we have a lot of function-calls with structured outputs. 01:24 Priya: yes, function/tool calling is supported. the main parity items are: function schema mapping, argument serialization; we recommend keeping the same JSON schema and just map the call payload. also our Console will show function taxonomy per model so you can audit. 01:38 Laura: embeddings - we send to Together for cheaper costs. how does redwood's embedding pricing and performance compare? 01:45 Jordan: Redwood offers curated embedding models; you can either use hosted embeddings (pay per unit) or route to Dedicated with lower unit cost. for parity, vector dimensions and similarity semantics are similar, but small float differences can change recall, we recommend reindexing and a small eval suite. 02:05 Priya: Optimize will give you quantization suggestions if you move to dedicated. we prepared a demo of auto-batching impact. 02:12 Priya: demoing console now -- (screen share described) route configuration, pinning model versions, canary rollouts, fallback policy to cheaper model if latency spikes. 02:30 Jordan: customer question often: latency vs cost. if you need 50ms p99, dedicated is typical; hosted can get close but is variable. 02:41 Michael: our SLA requirement is 200ms p95 for chat. what's realistic? 02:46 Priya: for 200ms we're in hosted's sweet spot for short contexts, but if your token counts spike you'll want dedicated autoscaling. Also caching helps: prefix caching can cut token cost by 20-40%. 03:05 Laura: security - we need SOC2 and KMS integration and SSO. can you do SAML with SCIM? 03:12 Jordan: yes, SSO/SAML + SCIM supported for Console. for keys and encryption we integrate with customer KMS for Private/Dedicated; hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS on enterprise plan. SOC 2 report we can share. 03:28 Michael: any gotchas migrating prompts? we have prompt templates with few-shot examples. 03:33 Priya: mostly the same, but temperature/top_p scaling differs; we can produce a parity mapping doc with suggested param tweaks per model and example prompts. also watch token counting differences. 03:48 Samir: what about SDK changes? we call OpenAI Python SDK and JS. 03:53 Priya: we have drop-in client libs with minimal changes; for node/python it's usually a change of endpoint and small rename of fields. we included a compatibility shim example in the mapping doc. 04:10 Jordan: cost comparison - we can run a benchmark. recommended PoC is 5M tokens across your top 10 prompts to collect latency/cost/quality. 04:20 Michael: timeline - we need this done before Q4 rollout. 04:23 Jordan: got it. we'll aim to have benchmark in 2 weeks. 04:27 Laura: what about rate limits and concurrency? we have bursts. 04:31 Priya: Redwood routing supports burst capacity and dedicated pools. you can set per-route concurrency limits and queueing. fallback to lower-cost model can be automatic. 04:45 Samir: any performance regressions with quantized models? 04:48 Priya: quantization trades a little quality; Optimize recommends which layers and bit-depths to use; for many use cases int8 works fine but for safety-critical outputs we keep float16. 04:59 Jordan: question about audit logs - we need per-request logs for compliance. 05:03 Priya: logs are available in Console, can be streamed to your SIEM or exported for retention. 05:12 Michael: are you able to run our benchmark in our VPC? 05:15 Jordan: yes, for Private we can deploy in your VPC or set up a dedicated peering. that takes a little more config but it's common. 05:25 Laura: ok demo looks good. can you also show Optimize reports? 05:29 Priya: yes, quick screenshot: Optimize shows per-route token breakdown, batching opportunities, cache hit rate, and model quantization suggestions. 05:45 Jordan: note: some transcription note - we sometimes mis-parse 'kv cache' as 'k v cache' in exported transcripts, ignore that. 05:52 Michael: objections - our procurement needs T&Cs around data residency and indemnity. 05:56 Jordan: we'll share enterprise legal terms with data residency notes; most customers include Addendum for EU residency. 06:06 Priya: last bit - rollout and monitoring: you can do canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on quality regression (we tie regression to your eval set). 06:18 Samir: sounds good. 06:22 Jordan: recap: we'll send parity mapping doc, schedule PoC benchmark, share SOC2 and security docs, and provide pricing for dedicated. 06:31 Michael: thanks, looking forward. 06:33 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with next steps. 06:37 (call ends) note: transcript has occasional mis-attributions and small typos as typical from auto-transcribe
